title: Oboe
summary: Limits first: the reed is assembled, not measured; its mass, resonance and face area are borrowed or assumed, none printed. Since the reed's closure stop (a857c6f17) the scale sits -7 to +33 c from equal temperament (F4 at its printed pressure only); before it, 22 to 158 c flat. At the pages' 7.4 kPa F4 plays an octave up (677 Hz). The old flat scale was the reed passing through its lay. There is no tongue; only the first open hole has a nonlinear loss, a quasi-steady orifice, and the breath noise row on Bb4, Db4, D4, F4, D5, G5 and Ab5 drives only 10 to 20 kHz on this reed's 0.87 mm duct. A C major scale and Ode to Joy are up, each note its own render at the pages' 7.4 kPa except F4, at its printed 6865 Pa, on fingerings inferred from Table III of Nederveen and de Bruijn 1967, the one complete oboe tone-hole table we hold. Bb4 (6 of 15) and Db4 (4 of 14, strict 3, with the contraction row below) are graded pages re-rendered after the stop, and Bb4 now sounds as B4, 99 c sharp of its name; G5 and Ab5 play an octave down and have no grade; D4, F4 and D5 are first pages at their printed pressures. A staple pressure recovery row (Almeida, Vergez and Caussé 2007; C_P 0.8 and S_c 4 mm^2, one measured reed's two numbers, borrowed; commit b57b46619) is on the D4 and D5 pages: D4, which does not speak at 6178 Pa without it, speaks with it (301.95 Hz, 48 c sharp of D4; ungraded, a listening page). The D5 page also carries the clarinet's bore air temperature profile (Noreland 2013, measured on a clarinet and borrowed for the oboe, positions rescaled), the mutual radiation impedance of the open holes and the bell, the printed thick-wall hole lengths of Lefebvre and Scavone, and, as a labelled bound trial, a jet contraction row (`contraction 0.611`, the two-dimensional free-streamline bound pi/(pi+2); commit 25b9bc64c): no double-reed value is printed, and the card's reed area, if it was fitted to a measured flow, already holds the contraction, so 0.611 is an upper bound on the row's effect and not a coefficient of this reed; the channel's unsteady inertance has no printed effective length and is not in the row. The page sounds at 578.17 Hz, D5 -27.2 c (from -73.1 c without any of the five rows, and 571.12 Hz, -48.5 c, with the first four), and scores 5 of 14, 3 on the strict ruler, against 4 and 3 for the page without the contraction row: the row brings the spectral flux inside the loose ruler, while the spectral distance, the third-octave envelope, the harmonic levels, the wavelet and cepstral gaps, odd against even and the centroid all widen, and the page is 5.1 dB quieter (96.5 dB SPL against 101.6). The same card without the staple row scored 5 of 14, so on D5 the staple row costs one measure (spectral flux) and brings the pitch 15 c nearer the recording. The staple row lowered the count on Db4 (3 to 2) and Bb4 (6 to 5), so those pages stay without it. The contraction row (0.611, the same bound trial as on D5, on the live card with no other row) raised the Db4 count from 3 to 4 of 14 and the strict count stayed at 3: the page sounds at 280.73 Hz, 22.0 c sharp of Db4 and 33.1 c sharp of the recording (the page without the row, 275.08 Hz, was 2.0 c from the recording), so the pitch measure is lost from both rulers and odd against even from the strict one, while the partial frequencies and the attack come inside both rulers and the harmonics-to-noise reading flips from 27.6 dB below the recording to 14.0 dB above it; the page is 4.8 dB quieter (97.8 dB SPL against 102.6) and the spectral, envelope, harmonic-level and wavelet gaps widen slightly. The same row on Bb4 lowered the count from 6 to 5 of 15 (strict 5 to 4), so the Bb4 page stays without it. On F4 the staple row moved the register edge below the printed pressure (the page plays 676 Hz, the second register, at 6865 Pa), so F4 stays as it is; G5 and Ab5 were not re-rendered with it. Eb6 has no render because the printed ladder ends at D5.
physics_present: generic fs-duct conical and cylindrical segments, tone-hole side branches and a flanged bell load, the lumped single-reed owner and the physical baffled outlet receiver already run for the clarinet; a description gives them this bore and a reed with values partly borrowed from the clarinet, and the posted first renders come from it

flow noise at the reed on Bb4, Db4, D4, F4, D5, G5 and Ab5 (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, extrapolated), with the card's first bore record, 0.87 mm, as its duct radius, by the clarinet cards' rule. At that radius it drives only 10 to 20 kHz, and the code takes the open-area ratio as 0 where this reed's is about 0.8
Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures for two professional oboe players are retained as player data

Fingerings chained from Table III's closed and open tones for each hole: inferred, not printed, from C4 to C5 and on the page notes. Where the table prints two rows for a note, the scale takes one and says which; the octave aids, holes 1, 2 and 5, aren't printed and are closed
A rigid, inelastic reed closure stop at zero opening (commit a857c6f17)

Quasi-steady orifice loss at the first open tone hole: a pressure drop K |U| U with K = rho / (2 C_vc^2 A_h^2), C_vc = 0.61 (c_d 2.69, the free-streamline bound for a sharp edge) and no threshold velocity; no other open hole has one

Staple pressure recovery of the double reed (Almeida, Vergez and Caussé 2007, eqs. 14-17; commit b57b46619), on the D4 and D5 pages: the blade is driven by the pressure drop across the opening and the bore input is raised by C_P (1/2) rho (q/S_c)^2, with C_P 0.8 and S_c 4e-6 m^2, one measured oboe reed's numbers (Figs 14 and 15), borrowed, not this reed's; it neglects the viscous loss along the reed, as this card does

Bore air temperature and humidity profile along the bore on the D5 page: a continuous gas field of the exhaled-breath mixture (Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969) with the clarinet cards' 14 stations from Noreland (2013), measured on a clarinet and borrowed for the oboe, only the positions rescaled by 0.634/0.655

Mutual radiation impedance between the open holes and the bell on the D5 page (TMMI, Lefebvre, Scavone and Kergomard 2013, half-space factor 2), distances along the bore axis only, an upper bound for holes on opposite sides
Printed thick-wall tone-hole lengths of Lefebvre and Scavone (2012) on the D5 page, in place of the engine's inner length

Vena contracta of the reed jet on the D5 and Db4 pages (the opt-in `contraction` row, commit 25b9bc64c; the contraction term of fs-phs GapFlowLaw without its channel terms, the staple law, where there is one, taken on the jet area; on Db4 the card has no staple row): C_c 0.611 = pi/(pi+2), the two-dimensional free-streamline bound, borrowed and a bound trial, not a measured coefficient of a double reed; the card's reed area may already hold it, so 0.611 is an upper bound on the row's effect
physics_missing: a measured bore profile and bell flare: only reads from the paper's graphs exist
pad and key heights, undercut geometry and a full fingering chart

a double-reed valve driving this bore: the paired-reed and material-modal valves exist in the engine, but the dense DG propagator's 2048-DOF cap refuses this bore. Its wall-loss fit needs 8 poles at the 0.87 mm reed tube, 13 to 16 at 2.4 mm, 17 to 20 at 5 mm and more than 32 at the 19 mm bell, and 8 poles alone put the 39-span bore and its 20 holes at 2124 DOF on the smallest mesh the grammar allows

staple and reed channel geometry (the pressure recovery law is in, with one measured reed's two numbers borrowed; this reed's staple is not measured; the jet contraction row is in, commit 25b9bc64c, with 0.611 borrowed as a bound, since no double reed's contraction is printed, and the channel's unsteady inertance is not in it, since no printed effective length of the channel is held)
a modern specimen: the only complete table is from 1967

A printed pressure for every note: Fuks and Sundberg print one for D4, F4, Bb4, D5 and F5 only, as a range (Table A6, two players, four dynamics, up and down); the pages use the second oboist's ff, rising. F4 (6865 Pa) plays in the first register and D5 (8041 Pa) speaks; Bb4 at 7551 Pa scored 5 of 15 against 6 and was not posted; D4 at 6178 Pa does not speak without the staple row and speaks with it; F5 has no printed fingering. Every other note uses the pages' 7.4 kPa

The scale's tuning. Before the reed's closure stop the scale was flat because the reed passed through its lay; with it the notes sit -7 to +33 c from equal temperament, F4 plays an octave up in the second register (nothing was done to bring it back), and Bb4 sounds as B4. The reed's blade mass, resonance and face area are borrowed or assumed, none printed: they need the authors or a measured reed

Nonlinear loss at the other open holes, and a printed coefficient for the first: c_d 2.69 is the code's free-streamline bound, not a printed value (printed: 2 for a tube end, 13/9 for a flanged end and 1.18 for a sharp hole in PVC, the last through a secondary source), and our hole edges aren't printed. On Bb4 the second open hole sits at the first one's station and carries the same flow, and the third about 0.6 of it, at the played note (the engine's small-signal transfer, not a render)

An oboe's own bore air temperature profile (the D5 page borrows a clarinet's), the holes' azimuths (the interaction takes axial distances only), and a way to give the Bb4 card's doubled hole its two openings: the engine refuses the interaction when two open holes sit at one axial station ("needs distinct finite opening stations"), so the Bb4 page cannot carry it. On D5 the three together moved the steady tone about 11 c and the level under 1 dB against the same card with a constant field, and the grader's count by one measure when the staple row was absent; with the staple row the count is the same as without them
blocked: The paper's bore graphs are read and its tables were transcribed from the page images, but no open source prints an oboe reed's blade mass, stiffness or damping. Needs those from the authors or a measured reed, and a newer measured oboe.
